cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and your strength moves out between people cleanly.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: At your practice today, settle what you're building toward, and aim the whole session there instead of ranging across everything.
cells.core:
You have a steady way of turning your strength outward, sharing what you carry with whoever can use it, and right now it is working. The practice has settled, and what you have cultivated shows up in what you can hand over. The small light you keep lit by attention is enough to be seen by.

Give the practice a heading. Decide what you are building toward — a skill, a number, a particular line of work — and let each session bend toward that rather than survey all of it. Wanting something specific is allowed, and it is what gives the sharing a shape a coworker or a friend can aim at. Direction doesn't narrow what you hand over; it makes handing it over intentional.
cells.sheetLine: You give well when you know what you're building toward.
cells.verb: sharing strength that flows between people by measure
cells.place: in the disciplined, repeated practice that turns intention into embodied skill

cells.tense: You are braced for a day that is not here yet, and the strength spills into it early.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: When somebody's owed a small thing and your gut says settle it, do that today without writing it in the tally.
cells.core:
You are working from the idea that if you don't hold everything up, it comes down. The practice has turned into a night watch, and the sharing has turned into supplying. What you are bracing against has not happened. From your seat the work looks like staying on top of a bad day whose outline you can already feel, and the strength you push at the room lands harder than you intended.

Let your own sense of what's fair settle the small case. When a little thing is owed — a reply, a fiver, something borrowed — do what seems right and skip the log. Fairness that moves doesn't keep count. Your grip can ease one notch and the room stays standing, because your strength was the steady part, not the force in it.
cells.sheetLine: Loosen the grip and the room still stands.
cells.verb: sharing strength that flows between people by measure
cells.place: in the disciplined, repeated practice that turns intention into embodied skill

cells.tense: You are still standing in front of a door you already walked through.
cells.act: drop the wrong approach and keep the commitment
cells.ask: Take a single piece of your practice that has stopped working, set just that piece down, and keep the practice going.
cells.core:
The practice went quiet somewhere in the last stretch. What you were building toward faded, and the sharing that used to flow got shut down in a way you did not quite author yourself. From where you sit the strength looks gone. Underneath, the commitment is still there, waiting on a way of doing it that no longer fits who you are now.

Let the friction show you what to drop, not what to abandon. Take a method that isn't working — an hour, a tool, the shape of the routine — and set it down. Keep the commitment itself. When something has genuinely finished, releasing it isn't defeat. The practice is clearing space for the next thing it will carry.
cells.sheetLine: What you're committed to can outlive how you were doing it.

cells.tense: The practice is already being steered, and the heading has not been written anywhere yet.
cells.act: decide the heading from what you want, not from logic
cells.ask: Pick the point of your session by what you actually want, not by the sensible argument, and put that line in the notebook.
cells.core:
You have been shaping the practice by what seems reasonable — the schedule, the argument, the sensible step — while something in you has been moving toward a different mark. Were you asked, you would say you were following the logic. The practice is following a want. The direction is being written by your own hand, and nobody has signed it, you included.

Name it. Before the session starts, settle what the whole thing is for out of what you actually want — the skill, the person, the version of yourself you have in mind — and put that line in the notebook. The line does the acknowledging. Once the heading is on paper, the strength you share has a reason the person receiving it can see.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering it already. One line makes it yours.
cells.verb: sharing strength that flows between people by measure
cells.place: in the disciplined, repeated practice that turns intention into embodied skill

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in each draft is that the person's support actually reaches the people around them; from the seat alone I cannot know whether their strength is already shared or kept. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not supporting anyone right now — I'm just being asked to.' The asks all survive that doubt because each is one small doable motion that teaches something even if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves the writer is any line that praises the person for how hard they hold on; I have kept the strands plain and left the 'why' out.
